Stan is an OpenCV, OpenAL based speech recognition engine designed for the web and for Flash.

Features include:

- Speech recognition in just a few minutes.
- Saves the entire recognition duration, including silences.
- Supports all human languages including multiple dialects.
- You can train it to better recognize your own accent.
- Uses real-time processing techniques to keep your system responsive.
- Uses simple REST-like syntax for communication with server (JSON).
- Records speech using microphone input with quality sampling rate (44.1 kHz).
- Recognizes speech using Google Web Speech API.
- Single C++ library, compiled for 32-bit Windows, 64-bit Linux and Mac OS X.
- JavaScript API.
- Flash client.
- Support for mobile devices.

See http://stan.relisten.net for more details and screenshots.

# How does it work?

While listening, data are read from the sound card, passed to the Stanford
Acoustic Model for real-time speech recognition and the result is outputted to
standard output. The response is formatted as plain text and can be sent to any
compatible web server to serve to a web-based client.

# Prerequisites

Before you can compile and use Stanford, you'll need the following:

- [Android NDK](http://developer.android.com/tools/sdk/ndk/index.html) (for Android support, optional)
- [Flash SDK](http://www.adobe.com/products/flashplayer/sdk/) (for Flash client support, optional)
- [CMake](http://www.cmake.org) (which comes with a precompiled binary for Windows available on their website)
- [VirtualBox](https://www.virtualbox.org/) (allows running Linux VM environment for compiling OpenCV, OpenAL emulators for Android without a Mac)
- [Ubuntu](http://www.ubuntu.com) Linux (64-bit tested initially, but also should work on 32-bit)
- A Mac is also required for compiling for MacOS X  (OpenCV & OpenAL, Flash SDK, CMake).

# Platforms

Stan supports the following platforms:

- **Windows 7+**: 32-bit & 64-bit
- **macOS 10.8+**: all platform, but only for 64-bit.
- **iOS**: 32-bit & 64-bit.
- **Android via VirtualBox**: 32-bit & 64-bit (not recommended for real devices)

# Build Instructions

## For 64-bit Linux:

In your terminal:

```sh
# download Android SDK/NDK (optional, but required for Android support)
wget https://dl.google.com/android/repository/android-ndk-r17-linux-x86_64.zip
wget https://dl.google.com/android/studio/android-studio-ide-171.4443003-linux.zip
# download VirtualBox (optional, required for Android support)
wget https://download.virtualbox.org/virtualbox/6.0.6/VirtualBox-6.0-6_0_6_123096_Ubuntu_amd64.deb
# clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/relistennet/stan.git
cd stan
mkdir build && cd build
# generate makefile
cmake ..
# compile the program
make
# run the program
./stan
```

## For Windows or macOS:

From your command prompt, with CMake, Git and Visual Studio installed:

```sh
# clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/relistennet/stan.git
cd stan
mkdir build && cd build
# generate solution
cmake ..

```

Press the build button. Follow the instructions on the [CMake Documentation Page](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/v3.12/guide/building_cmake-generated-file.html#build-a-project-in-visual-studio) for instructions on building the project in Visual Studio.

On macOS, the Terminal program comes with Xcode. Xcode needs to be installed from the App Store first.

For more platform specifics visit the [Wiki Page](https://github.com/relistennet/stan/wiki/Platform-Dependencies).

The following command line options are available that control the build:

* `-DUSE_ANDROID=TRUE` - builds SDL (SDL2 to be more precise) from source with POSIX variant for the Android build. Android build takes very long time because it has to build SDL from source code.

* `-DOPENAL_LIBRARY=/path/to/openal` - path to an OpenAL library (only if precompiled binaries for your platform are not available)

If you have set the Android NDK path, you need to set `-DANDROID_NDK=/path/to/android-ndk`.

You can also set `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug/Release`. Debug is not recommended for releases.

```python
class Knight:
    def __init__(self, color, position):
        self.color = color
        self.position = position

    def __str__(self):
        return "{} Knight at {}".format(self.color, self.position)

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return self.color == other.color and self.position == other.position

    def move(self, size, new_position):
        self.directions = [(1, 2), (2, 1), (2, -1), (1, -2),
                           (-1, -2), (-2, -1), (-2, 1), (-1, 2)]
        self.possible_moves = []

        for direction in self.directions:
            new_row = self.position[0] + direction[0]
            new_column = self.position[1] + direction[1]

            if 0 <= new_row < size and 0 <= new_column < size:
                if abs(new_row - new_position[0]) <= 1 and abs(
                        new_column - new_position[1]) <= 1:
                    self.possible_moves.append((new_row, new_column))
        return self.possible_moves
```

This SDK has two components - the logical model, and the backend-specific implementations. The backend-specific implementations are used to retrieve and manipulate the data itself, corresponding to the objects defined in `sdk-dm`. The release involves branching off the repository from the current `master` branch, setting a new version in the `develop`, and `prerelease` versions are published to NPM (tagging `beta`) so they can be tested in production. Stan is an OpenCV, OpenAL based speech recognition engine designed for the web and for Flash.

Features include:

- Speech recognition in multiple languages
- Supports ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) and OCR (Optical Character Recognition)
- Handles streams including multiple speakers
- Supports a variety of speech input sources including microphone, file, webcams, and video files
- Outputs results via text, speech, simple events, and async/wait
- Scriptable recognition events
- Handles multiple simultaneous recognizers on a single machine
- Utility scripts for working with corpora, handling speaker training data, converting flac files to the proper format, etc. 
- Supports timed speech recognition: user specifies a starting and ending time for recognition and the engine will stop when it has recognized everything the user wants
- Loads trained models for recognition

You can find documentation and user guides in the [wiki](https://github.com/RelistenNet/stan/wiki) for this project.

Supports ASR and OCR technologies:

- [Kaldi](http://kaldi-asr.org/)
- [Mozilla DeepSpeech](http://mozilla.github.io/DeepSpeech/)
- [Google Web Speech API](https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2014/01/Web-apps-that-talk--The-webkitspeechrecognition-API)
- [CMU Sphinx](http://cmusphinx.sourceforge.net/)

Note: The Kaldi-based recognizer is not currently maintained, please use the Mozilla DeepSpeech or Google Web Speech API based engines instead.

For support or questions, please join the [Discourse](https://discourse.relisten.net/).

Installation
------------

Most of the time, installation will happen via npm (node package manager). First, make sure you have a recent version of NodeJs installed.

```
npm install stan
```

If you're using this in a browser, there's a build for Stan available in the [dist](https://github.com/RelistenNet/stan/tree/dist) directory that you can host yourself.

The first time you run Stan in standalone mode (not inside a voice.js instance), you'll need to create a model directory and download a set of models into it. This can be done with the following commands:

```
mkdir models
node scripts/download-models.js
```

Test it:

```
node test/test.js
```

Additional Information
----------------------

Please see the [wiki](https://github.com/RelistenNet/stan/wiki) and [issues](https://github.com/RelistenNet/stan/issues) for additional information and a roadmap.

This project is developed, tested and maintained by a team of researchers from the University of Washington. We are interested in improving this project and are actively looking for more contributors!

Do you have a problem that you're solving with speech recognition/OCR? Or maybe you're just interested in learning more about it? Let us know! We'd love to help you get started.
